To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency of nonlinear optical processes in metamaterials is not only determined by their linear optical properties, but also by collective effects.

the second harmonic generation (SHG) efficiency from a periodic array of split ring resonators (SRRs) exhibits a nonmonotonical dependence on lattice constant and that the SHG efficiency from an SRR array can be enhanced by a factor of 2.7 compared to the SHG from a single SRR by using a lattice constant of 2.5 times the diameter of a single SRR.

the conversion efficiency of second harmonic generation from a split ring resonator array is not a monotonous function of the lattice constant and can be understood in terms of a dilution effect and linewidth changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of metamaterials and their application to optical devices.
the study of the optical properties of plasmonic metamaterials.
the study of nonlinear optical effects in metamaterials and metasurfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the second harmonic generation from the SRR array is dominated by the near field interaction between the SRRs and that the dilution effects can be neglected.

the second harmonic generation from a square array of split ring resonators shows a nonmonotonical dependence on the lattice constant due to a competition between the dilution and interaction effects.
the second harmonic generation from a split ring resonator array is not only a result of the individual resonator response but also due to the inter-element interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nonlinear response of metamaterials can be tuned by varying the array lattice constant, and that this tuning is not only due to the modification of the linear response, but also to the modification of nonlinear susceptibilities due to interactions among elements.
the nonlinear response of the metamaterials is not only determined by the individual resonators but also by collective effects.
the second harmonic generation efficiency from a split ring resonator array is a nontrivial function of the lattice constant and the array size.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the case of second harmonic generation, the nonlinear susceptibility of the split ring resonator array is not simply a weighted sum of the individual nonlinear susceptibilities of the individual split ring resonators, but also depends on the lattice constant of the array.
collective effects in metamaterial arrays are not always negligible, even in the limit of weak interactions.
collective effects in nonlinear metamaterials can be used to tailor the nonlinear response of metamaterials.
